findings.issue_text: [BUG] The diff adds backupCode to the LoginValues interface but never adds it to the zod formSchema that zodResolver parses the login form with, so zod strips the unknown key and the submit handler calls signIn('Cal.com', {...values}) without any backupCode field. A locked-out user who enters a valid backup code on the login page gets a silent no-op: authorize() receives no backupCode, falls into the TOTP branch, throws SecondFactorRequired, and the response handler only calls setTwoFactorRequired(true) — the user stays on the backup-code screen with no error message, and the new IncorrectBackupCode/MissingBackupCodes handlers added in this same diff are unreachable dead code on the login path.

[BUG] After rerouting successful enablement through SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes, onEnable() is now only invoked from the backup-codes 'close' button, so dismissing the dialog via Escape or an overlay click at that step closes it without calling onEnable() or resetState(). 2FA is fully enabled server-side but the parent's post-enable update that onEnable() performs never runs, so the security settings UI keeps showing two-factor authentication as disabled (and the modal's internal step stays on DisplayBackupCodes) until a full page reload.

[ADVISORY] The two new server-side backup-code paths — the backup branch in next-auth authorize() and the backup branch in totp/disable — ship with zero test coverage in this diff; the added e2e steps only exercise code display/download/copy, and the diff's own TODO defers 'login + disabling 2fa with backup'. Regressions in those branches ship silently — and one already has: the zod-stripping defect that makes backup-code login a silent no-op is exactly what the deferred login test would have caught.

[ADVISORY] The new backup-code component's internal function is named TwoFactor ('export default function TwoFactor' inside BackupCode.tsx), duplicating the name of the adjacent auth/TwoFactor.tsx component it is toggled against in the same modals. Stack traces, React DevTools and profiler output label the backup-code input as 'TwoFactor', and searching TwoFactor usages now returns a second unrelated component in the same directory, misleading anyone debugging the 2FA/backup-code toggle flows.

[BUG] The zod formSchema consumed by the login form's zodResolver is never updated to include the new backupCode field (the diff only extends the LoginValues interface, the BackupCode input registration, and the next-auth provider credentials config), so zodResolver strips backupCode from the handleSubmit values before signIn is called. A user who lost their authenticator enters a valid backup code on the login page, but the credentials POST carries no backupCode; next-auth's authorize falls into the TOTP branch and returns SecondFactorRequired, which the handler treats as 'reveal the 2FA input' — the user stays on the backup-code screen with no error message and cannot log in. The diff's own e2e TODO ('login + disabling 2fa with backup') confirms this path was never exercised.

[BUG] The new missing_backup_codes message instructs users to 'generate them in your settings', but the diff adds no settings UI or API action to (re)generate backup codes for an account that already has 2FA enabled. Existing 2FA users (backupCodes is null after the migration) and users who never saved their codes hit a dead end: the only code-generating endpoint (setup.ts) also resets twoFactorEnabled to false and rotates the TOTP secret, i.e. a full disable-and-re-setup, and no regeneration entry point is added for enabled users. On the login page the instruction is shown to a locked-out user who by definition cannot reach settings.

[ADVISORY] No test in the diff exercises the two new server-side branches — backup-code verification/consumption in next-auth-options.ts authorize() and the backup-code path in totp/disable.ts; the only test file touched carries the author's own TODO deferring exactly those flows (searched diff for test-shaped files: only login.2fa.e2e.ts and the builder.ts fixture, which contains no assertions). A regression in single-use consumption, the dash-stripping comparison, or the MissingBackupCodes guard ships silently; the added e2e only clicks download/copy/close and explicitly TODOs the file-content and clipboard-content checks further down in the same hunk.

[ADVISORY] Dismissing the dialog at the DisplayBackupCodes step (Escape, outside click, or the DialogContent close affordance) passes straight through onOpenChange with no guard, and nothing in the diff can ever re-display those codes. A user who enables 2FA and dismisses the dialog without clicking download/copy loses the only plaintext rendering of the codes; they remain stored encrypted with no re-view endpoint (setup.ts only regenerates as part of a full re-setup that rotates the secret), so the codes are effectively lost and the user is one phone loss away from the dead-end missing_backup_codes state.

[BUG] Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write (decrypt → indexOf → prisma.user.update) with no transaction or optimistic lock, so two concurrent logins with the same code both pass verification and a lost update can resurrect an already-consumed code. Two simultaneous sign-ins with the same code both succeed (each writes back its own copy of the array), violating the 'each backup code can be used exactly once' promise stated in backup_code_instructions; interleaved writes using different codes can re-add a code nulled by the other request, leaving a 'used' code valid again.

[BUG] Backup-code matching is exact and case/whitespace-sensitive (indexOf on the dash-stripped raw input) while the generated codes are lowercase hex, with no toLowerCase/trim normalization server-side and no autoCapitalize/autoCorrect/spellCheck suppression on the BackupCode input. A user transcribing a valid code in uppercase — e.g. a mobile keyboard auto-capitalizing the first character, or manual entry from a printed sheet — gets 'Backup code is incorrect' and remains locked out despite possessing a valid code; the identical raw comparison exists in totp/disable.ts.

[ADVISORY] The copy button shows the 'Backup codes copied!' success toast unconditionally; navigator.clipboard.writeText is fire-and-forget, so a rejected clipboard write still reports success. When the browser denies clipboard permission (or navigator.clipboard is unavailable in an insecure context and writeText throws), the user is told the codes were copied, may skip saving them another way, and only discovers the loss the next time they need a backup code.

[ADVISORY] The new backup-code branch dereferences req.body.backupCode with replaceAll and JSON.parses the decrypted blob with no type guard or try/catch, so a non-string backupCode or a corrupt/undecryptable stored payload throws out of the handler. A POST with backupCode as a number/object (or a user row encrypted under a rotated CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY) produces an unhandled TypeError and an opaque 500 instead of a 4xx; the same unguarded JSON.parse pattern is copied into next-auth-options.ts, where it surfaces as a generic login failure.

[ADVISORY] Setting tabIndex={-1} on the password-visibility toggle inside the shared PasswordField removes it from keyboard tab order for every password field in the app, not just the 2FA modals motivating the change. Keyboard-only users can no longer reach the show/hide toggle on any PasswordField (login, signup, all settings password forms); the modal focus annoyance is fixed at the cost of an app-wide accessibility regression on a shared UI primitive.

[ADVISORY] The vacuous assertion the new FIXME comment itself calls out — expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy() receives a Promise object, which is always truthy — is left in place guarding the fixture's 2FA-enabled state. The shared 2FA fixture can proceed with the two-factor switch unchecked, so every test depending on 'user has 2FA enabled' can silently run against a user without 2FA; the diff documents the broken check instead of fixing it while touching these exact lines.

[BUG] The feature ships no way to generate or regenerate backup codes outside the initial 2FA setup flow (setup.ts is the only writer of user.backupCodes in this diff), yet the new MissingBackupCodes copy tells users to 'generate them in your settings' — a capability that does not exist anywhere in the diff. Every user who enabled 2FA before this deploy has backupCodes=null; when they use the new 'Lost access' recovery path (login.tsx or DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx), the server returns missing-backup-codes (disable.ts:55, next-auth-options.ts:136) and the message sends them to a settings page with no generate action. The exact population backup codes exist to rescue — users locked out of their authenticator — gets a dead end with a false instruction, since the setup endpoint that generates codes is unreachable without completing a login.

[ADVISORY] Scope drift: the PR changes the shared PasswordField in packages/ui to remove the show/hide toggle from tab order (tabIndex={-1}), altering keyboard behavior for every password field in the app, not just the 2FA flows this feature covers. All PasswordField consumers (login, signup, password change, EE modals) silently lose keyboard access to the visibility toggle — an app-wide behavior change bundled invisibly under a '2fa backup codes' PR and untraceable to any backup-code requirement; it should be its own change or scoped to the new modal.

[BUG] The 'each backup code can be used exactly once' invariant is not enforced atomically: authorize reads the decrypted list, matches indexOf, then writes the re-encrypted list in a separate non-transactional update, so two concurrent sign-ins with the same code both read the pre-consumption list and both succeed. A backup code is redeemable twice under concurrent use, contradicting the user-facing promise in backup_code_instructions ('exactly once'); a leaked code retains full value after its first legitimate use.

[BUG] Enabling 2FA no longer completes on success: handleEnable replaces the previous unconditional onEnable() call with setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes), leaving the explicit 'Close' button as the only path that fires onEnable() and resetState(). Dismissing the dialog via Escape, overlay click, or the dialog's built-in close control on the backup-codes step skips onEnable(), so the settings page keeps showing 2FA as disabled after a successful enable until reload, and skips resetState(), so the modal reopens on the stale DisplayBackupCodes step with the password still held in component state.

[BUG] disable.ts calls req.body.backupCode.replaceAll('-','') after only a truthiness check, so any non-string JSON value in the body (number, boolean, object) throws a TypeError and produces a 500 instead of a 4xx. An authenticated POST to /api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable with {"backupCode": 123} from a user with stored backup codes crashes the handler (123.replaceAll is not a function) — an unhandled 500 on an auth endpoint; the next-auth path is unaffected only because NextAuth credentials are always strings.

[BUG] Backup-code matching is case-sensitive end to end: codes are lowercase hex (crypto.randomBytes(5).toString('hex')) and both comparison sites (next-auth-options.ts:143 and disable.ts:61) call indexOf without any toLowerCase normalization, while the input placeholder 'XXXXX-XXXXX' suggests uppercase and mobile keyboards auto-capitalize the first character. A user who manually types a valid code containing any uppercase letter (e.g., the first character auto-capitalized on iOS) gets 'Backup code is incorrect' and stays locked out despite holding a valid recovery code; copy-paste from the download works, manual entry silently fails.

[ADVISORY] The security-critical backup-code verification and single-use consumption logic added in next-auth-options.ts and disable.ts has no test coverage in this diff — the e2e file's own TODO defers 'login + disabling 2fa with backup', and the new e2e steps only click download/copy/close with TODOs for asserting file and clipboard content. A regression in the consumption logic (code never nulled, wrong index written, or re-encryption corrupting the stored JSON array) ships silently; backup-code login and backup-code disable — the two paths that can bypass or surrender TOTP — are entirely untested.

[ADVISORY] The backup-code decrypt→parse→indexOf verification block is duplicated as hand-maintained copies in next-auth-options.ts:130-144 and disable.ts:47-64, and the copies have already drifted (authorize consumes the used code; disable relies on the later null-out; error handling differs between throw and res.status). The next change to matching semantics (e.g., the missing case normalization) must be found and applied in two places; missing one leaves login and disable enforcing different code formats for the same stored codes.

[ADVISORY] The new BackupCode component's default export is still named TwoFactor (export default function TwoFactor), a copy-paste remnant from the component it was cloned from. React DevTools trees, error stack frames, and grep for TwoFactor now resolve to the backup-code component, misleading anyone debugging the login or disable-2FA flows into editing the wrong file.

[BUG] Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write: authorize decrypts the whole blob, nulls one index in JS, and overwrites the column with no transaction, lock, or atomic update, so two concurrent logins with the same code both succeed and two concurrent logins with different codes resurrect an already-consumed code. The 'each backup code can be used exactly once' contract (stated in backup_code_instructions) breaks under concurrency: N parallel requests carrying one stolen code yield N sessions, and a concurrent second-code login writes back a blob that restores a burned code to validity — a lost update on a security credential.

[BUG] Dismissing the dialog at the DisplayBackupCodes step via ESC or overlay click fires onOpenChange without calling onEnable or resetState (only the in-step Close button does), so the parent is left believing 2FA is still disabled after the server has enabled it. After a successful enable, an ESC/overlay dismissal closes the modal with no success callback: the settings UI keeps showing 2FA as disabled until an external refetch, the success toast never fires, and the modal retains stale step/backupCodes state so reopening it shows the backup-codes step again.

[BUG] The backup-code comparison is case-sensitive while generation produces lowercase hex (crypto.randomBytes(5).toString('hex')) and user input is only dash-stripped, never lowercased, so a code entered with any uppercase character misses indexOf and returns IncorrectBackupCode. A legitimate user who enters their recovery code with uppercase letters is told the code is incorrect and is locked out of the recovery path; disable.ts line 61 contains the identical case-sensitive comparison.

[ADVISORY] Backup codes are modeled as one encrypted JSON array in a nullable TEXT column with per-code state encoded as null sentinels inside the blob, instead of a child table with per-code hash and used_at. Consumption must decrypt-modify-re-encrypt the entire blob (the direct cause of the lost-update race in next-auth-options.ts), no single code can be consumed atomically, and there is no audit trail of which code was used when; a backup_codes(userId, codeHash, usedAt) child table would make consumption one atomic UPDATE and give an audit trail.

[ADVISORY] The backup-code verification block (decrypt, JSON.parse, dash-stripped indexOf) is duplicated verbatim in the disable endpoint (disable.ts lines 58-66), and the two copies already diverge on consumption semantics — login nulls one code, disable deletes all. The next change to code matching (case normalization, length check, error code) lands in one copy and silently drifts from the other, giving login and disable different acceptance rules for the same credential.

[ADVISORY] The new backup-code component's default export is named TwoFactor, colliding with the identically-named default export in TwoFactor.tsx. React DevTools, stack traces, and greps for 'TwoFactor' now resolve to two different components with adjacent semantics; the pair is disambiguated only by file path, so a future import or refactor can bind the wrong component.

[ADVISORY] The diff's own TODO records that the new server paths — backup-code login with consumption in next-auth-options.ts and disable-via-backup-code in disable.ts — have no test coverage anywhere in this diff. A regression in the consume-on-login write or the disable branch (codes never nulled, or disable accepting an invalid code) ships green: CI exercises only the enable-flow display/download/copy/close buttons, so the single-use guarantee and the recovery path can break undetected.

[ADVISORY] The missing_backup_codes message instructs 'Please generate them in your settings', but the only generator in this diff is the setup endpoint, which is part of the enable flow and sets twoFactorEnabled: false. At login (where the message also renders) the user cannot reach settings at all, and in the disable modal the instruction is circular: generating codes requires the enable flow, which requires first disabling 2FA — the very thing the user is failing to do — so existing 2FA users with backupCodes=null are pointed at a path that does not exist.

[ADVISORY] The diff ships a FIXME documenting that the enable-flow assertion expect(...isChecked()).toBeTruthy() passes even when the switch is unchecked — a known false-green guard on the exact flow this PR modifies. The 2FA e2e suite can go green while the enable flow is broken in production; the author's own comment confirms the check verifies nothing until it is rewritten to the data-state selector used in the test below it.

[BUG] LoginValues gains backupCode but the zod formSchema consumed by zodResolver (line ~68) is not extended with a backupCode field anywhere in this diff, so zodResolver strips backupCode from the parsed values handed to signIn and a correctly entered code reaches NextAuth's authorize as undefined. authorize falls through to the TOTP branch with an empty totpCode and throws SecondFactorRequired, which the login page handles by merely re-showing the TOTP view with no error message — a locked-out user submitting a valid backup code gets a silent no-op (no login, no feedback), so the feature's core recovery path never works from the login page; the author's own e2e TODO confirms backup-code login is untested, so nothing catches this.

[BUG] handleEnable's success path now defers onEnable() to the DisplayBackupCodes close button (line ~269), but the Dialog still closes on ESC/outside-click via onOpenChange without invoking onEnable() or resetState(), silently changing when the parent is told the enable succeeded. The server has already set twoFactorEnabled=true, yet after a user dismisses the backup-codes screen with ESC the parent's onEnable callback never fires and the security settings view keeps reporting 2FA as disabled; the one-time code display is abandoned without the acknowledgment step the new flow mandates, and if the parent unmounts the modal on close the codes can never be viewed again (no re-view feature exists).

[ADVISORY] The migration adds backupCodes as a nullable column with no backfill, so every user who enabled 2FA before this deploy has backupCodes=null while the login page now shows them the 'Lost access' backup-code path. For that cohort the recovery path always dead-ends in MissingBackupCodes with the message 'No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings.' — an instruction a locked-out user at the login screen cannot follow, so the UI advertises a recovery objective the backend cannot fulfill for existing 2FA users.

[BUG] The backup-code TextField sets no autoCapitalize="none"/autoCorrect="off" while stored codes are lowercase hex (crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")), so iOS Safari's default sentence capitalization uppercases the first typed character and the server's case-sensitive indexOf comparison rejects a correctly typed code. A user in account recovery manually typing their valid backup code on an iPhone (the canonical cross-device scenario: codes displayed on one device, entered on another) gets 'Backup code is incorrect.' with no indication the keyboard mutated the input.

[ADVISORY] The backup-code verification sequence (encryption-key check, presence check, symmetricDecrypt+JSON.parse, dash-stripped indexOf) is duplicated verbatim in the authorize handler in next-auth-options.ts, creating two hand-maintained copies of a security check. Any future normalization or hardening fix (trim, case-folding, corrupted-ciphertext handling) applied to one copy silently skips the other, so login and disable drift into validating codes by different rules.

[ADVISORY] No test in the diff exercises backup-code login or backup-code-based 2FA disable — the added e2e coverage stops at the enable-flow download/copy/close buttons, and the TODO added at line 12 concedes the gap. A regression in the next-auth-options.ts authorize backup branch or the disable.ts backup branch (e.g., the stripped-field failure on the login form) ships undetected and locks users out of the recovery path the feature exists to provide.

[ADVISORY] tabIndex={-1} removes the password-visibility toggle from keyboard tab order for every PasswordField in the app — a shared-component behavior change bundled into this PR with no backup-codes-related necessity. Keyboard-only users can no longer reveal their password to verify it on the login, signup, and 2FA-disable forms; the change alters an app-wide accessibility contract without explicit acceptance.

[ADVISORY] The new component's default export is named TwoFactor inside BackupCode.tsx (copy-paste from TwoFactor.tsx), so the codebase now has two different default exports named TwoFactor. Anyone grepping for or importing TwoFactor hits both implementations; the next editor of this file risks patching the wrong component or importing the wrong one under an assumed name.

[BUG] login.tsx adds backupCode to the LoginValues interface but never adds it to the zod formSchema that zodResolver (line 67) parses on submit, so zod's default unknown-key stripping drops backupCode from the values handleSubmit hands to signIn and the credentials provider (which now accepts a backupCode credential, next-auth-options.ts line 64) never receives it from the login page. The new lost-access login flow is non-functional: a user who lost their authenticator enters a valid backup code, authorize sees credentials.backupCode undefined and falls into the TOTP branch, which throws SecondFactorRequired because totpCode was cleared by the Lost access handler, and login.tsx maps that error to setTwoFactorRequired(true) with no message — the user is silently bounced back to the backup-code screen in a loop and is locked out despite the UI advertising recovery; the IncorrectBackupCode/MissingBackupCodes handlers added at lines 156-157 are dead code on this page.

[BUG] disable.ts calls req.body.backupCode.replaceAll without validating that backupCode is a string, so any truthy non-string JSON body value (object, array, number, boolean) throws an uncaught TypeError at line 61. An authenticated user with 2FA enabled who POSTs {"backupCode": {}} (or any non-string) with their correct password crashes the handler and receives a 500 Internal Server Error instead of the 400 + ErrorCode response the endpoint's other branches promise; the same unvalidated .replaceAll exists on credentials.backupCode in next-auth-options.ts line 141 for clients that POST JSON to the credentials callback.

[ADVISORY] The backup-code consume step in authorize is a non-atomic read-modify-write (decrypt at 136-138, indexOf at 141, re-encrypt the whole array at 146-153) with no transaction, lock, or conditional write, so two concurrent sign-in requests presenting the same valid code both pass the indexOf check before either write lands. A backup code can be redeemed twice in parallel, creating two sessions from one code and violating the exactly-once invariant the new UI copy added in this diff ('Each backup code can be used exactly once') promises.

[ADVISORY] The migration adds backupCodes as a nullable column with no default or backfill, so every user who enabled 2FA before this deploy has backupCodes=null, and setup.ts (the only writer, requiring an authenticated session) is unreachable for them, so the new Lost access flow throws MissingBackupCodes for exactly the users most likely to need it. Pre-existing 2FA users who lose their authenticator click the advertised Lost access button, submit any code, and get 'No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings.' — an instruction they cannot follow while logged out, leaving them permanently locked out with no in-product recourse.

[ADVISORY] The codes rendered on the DisplayBackupCodes step come from the earlier setup response held in component state (setBackupCodes at line 92), not from the enable response, so they are not guaranteed to equal the codes currently stored server-side at the moment enable succeeds. If a second setup run interleaves (e.g., the user opens the enable modal in two tabs; the second setup overwrites the stored codes and secret while the first tab's enable still succeeds because the user's authenticator now holds the newer secret), the user archives the stale tab's codes and discovers they are invalid only when they need them for recovery — permanent lockout with codes that look valid.

[ADVISORY] The backup-code verification logic (decrypt with CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY, dash-stripping via replaceAll, indexOf match, IncorrectBackupCode/MissingBackupCodes error codes) is duplicated verbatim between disable.ts (58-63) and next-auth-options.ts (136-142) with no shared helper, so the two copies are already hand-maintained parallel implementations. Any future change to matching semantics (case-insensitivity, format tolerance, constant-time compare, per-code hashing) must be mirrored in both files; a fix applied to only one site silently creates inconsistent auth behavior where a code is accepted at login but rejected when disabling 2FA, and every reviewer must remember both sites.

[BUG] The assertion `await expect(page.locator('[data-testid=two-factor-switch]').isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` asserts nothing: `isChecked()` returns a Promise object, which is always truthy, so the expectation passes regardless of whether the switch is checked — a fact the diff's own added FIXME comment ('this passes even when switch is not checked') confirms while leaving the broken assertion in place. The test claims to verify that 2FA was actually enabled after the setup flow but passes even when enabling silently failed, giving false confidence that the 2FA setup step works; any regression that leaves the switch unchecked still yields a green suite.

[ADVISORY] The core single-use backup-code login path (decrypt stored codes, match, null out the consumed entry, re-encrypt and persist) has zero test coverage in this diff: the only test files touched are apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts — whose added TODO at line 13 explicitly admits 'login + disabling 2fa with backup' is untested — and packages/lib/test/builder.ts, which only adds a `backupCodes: null` default. A regression in the consume-once persistence (e.g., the prisma update failing silently or the re-encrypted array corrupting the remaining codes) would let a backup code be replayed indefinitely, breaking the feature's stated 'each backup code can be used exactly once' contract, and no test in this diff would catch it; an integration gap such as the login form's zod schema stripping the new `backupCode` field before it reaches `authorize()` would also ship undetected.

[ADVISORY] The new backup-code branch of the disable endpoint (encryption-key guard, MissingBackupCodes/IncorrectBackupCode responses, JSON.parse of the decrypted blob) has no test in this diff — the e2e suite still exercises only the TOTP disable path, and the added TODO in apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts line 13 acknowledges disabling with a backup code is untested. A regression here ships undetected: e.g., `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, ...))` throwing on legacy or corrupted stored data returns an unhandled 500 instead of the 4xx error codes the client's new `IncorrectBackupCode`/`MissingBackupCodes` branches in DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx expect, and the new DisableTwoFactorModal lost-access toggle flow is never driven by any test.

[ADVISORY] The new e2e assertions verify only that the download and copy actions fire — the download check asserts the filename but never the file content ('TODO: check file content'), and the copy check asserts a toast that EnableTwoFactorModal shows unconditionally (showToast runs after the non-awaited `navigator.clipboard.writeText`, so it appears even when the clipboard write rejects) — so the actual backup-code content produced by both paths is never asserted anywhere in the diff. A regression in `formatBackupCode` or the blob/clipboard serialization in EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx (codes without dashes, wrong count, empty file, silently failed clipboard write) passes the suite; the backup-code generation in setup.ts (10 codes of 10 hex chars) is likewise never content-verified by any test.

[ADVISORY] The migration adds backupCodes as a nullable column with no backfill, so every user whose 2FA was enabled before this deploy has backupCodes = NULL, and the new Lost Access flow dead-ends for exactly those users: authorize throws MissingBackupCodes and the login page renders 'No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings.' — an instruction a locked-out user cannot follow. Pre-existing 2FA users who lose their authenticator click the new 'Lost access' button, submit a code, and are sent in circles by the only recovery affordance the UI offers (they cannot log in to reach settings, and no generate path exists while 2FA is enabled even when logged in); the same misleading message renders in DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx (lines 75-76) for codeless logged-in users, where it is confusing but recoverable via the TOTP path.

[BUG] The diff adds backupCode to LoginValues and registers it via BackupCode's methods.register("backupCode"), but the zod formSchema that useForm resolves against (defined above line 65, untouched by this diff) has no backupCode key, so zodResolver strips the field from the parsed values handed to onSubmit. signIn("credentials") is called without backupCode; authorize falls into the TOTP branch and throws SecondFactorRequired, which the handler maps to setTwoFactorRequired(true) with no error message — a user entering a valid backup code at login gets neither a session nor any feedback (the form silently does nothing), so the entire lost-access recovery path this PR adds is non-functional at login.

[BUG] The copy button calls navigator.clipboard.writeText(...) without awaiting it or attaching a rejection handler, then unconditionally shows the "backup codes copied!" success toast on the next line. When the clipboard write rejects (permission denied, document unfocused) the user is told the copy succeeded while it failed, and the rejection is unhandled; backup codes are displayed exactly once, so a user who trusts the toast and closes the dialog can permanently lose their recovery codes.

[BUG] handleEnable replaces onEnable() with setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes), deferring the success signal to the backup-codes "close" button, while Escape/overlay dismissal exits the Dialog via onOpenChange only and never invokes onEnable (or resetState). Dismissing the dialog at the backup-codes step leaves the server with twoFactorEnabled=true while the parent is never notified and keeps showing 2FA as disabled; the natural recovery — clicking Enable again — re-runs the setup endpoint, which silently regenerates the TOTP secret and backup codes and invalidates the codes the user already saved.

[BUG] authorize persists the consumed backup code (backupCodes[index] = null followed by prisma.user.update) before the credentials flow has actually produced a session. Any failure after the burn — an error in NextAuth's jwt/session callbacks, a dropped response, or the client dying before the session cookie is set — leaves the user logged out with that backup code permanently destroyed; the retry now returns IncorrectBackupCode, so recovery codes are burned by attempts that never yielded access, with no audit trail or way to restore them.

[ADVISORY] The backup-code consumption is an unguarded read-modify-write (decrypt → indexOf → null → encrypt → update) with no transaction or compare-and-swap on the prior ciphertext. Two concurrent sign-ins using different valid codes both read the same stored list and the last write wins, restoring the first code into storage — a spent code silently remains valid and the stored state diverges from the codes actually used, breaking the "exactly once" promise the UI makes (double-submit races hit the same interleaving).

[BUG] The disable endpoint's new error log reads "Missing encryption key; cannot proceed with backup code login." although this handler is the 2FA disable endpoint, not login. Operators debugging a failed 2FA disable see a log naming the wrong flow and endpoint, misdirecting the investigation to the login path (the identical message in next-auth-options.ts is correct, so the copy-paste is detectable by comparison).

[BUG] The MissingBackupCodes error surfaced on the login page renders "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings.", instructing a locked-out user to perform an action that requires being logged in. The exact audience this message targets — users who lost their authenticator and have no backup codes — cannot reach settings, so the error misdirects them with an impossible remediation step instead of pointing at the real recovery options (the same message in DisableTwoFactorModal is equally unactionable, since generation only happens in the enable flow).

[BUG] The backup-code verification block calls req.body.backupCode.replaceAll and JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, ...)) with no type guard and no error handling. A truthy non-string backupCode (number, object, or array in the JSON body) throws TypeError on .replaceAll, and an undecryptable or corrupt backupCodes blob (e.g. after encryption-key rotation) throws inside JSON.parse — both escape as an unhandled 500 with a non-JSON body instead of the 400 {error: ErrorCode} envelope the modal's error mapping expects, so the client's response.json() throws and the user lands in the generic catch message.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Backup-code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write: authorize decrypts the whole blob, nulls one index in JS, and overwrites the column with no transaction, lock, or atomic update, so two concurrent logins with the same code both succeed and two concurrent logins with different codes resurrect an already-consumed code. The 'each backup code can be used exactly once' contract (stated in backup_code_instructions) breaks under concurrency: N parallel requests carrying one stolen code yield N sessions, and a concurrent second-code login writes back a blob that restores a burned code to validity — a lost update on a security credential.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, backup-code login does a non-atomic read-modify-write: it decrypts the full `user.backupCodes` blob, checks membership, mutates the JS array (`backupCodes[index] = null`), then overwrites the column via `prisma.user.update(...)` with no transaction or conditional/atomic update. This allows concurrent requests to both validate the same code (both read the pre-consumption blob) and also causes lost updates where two different-code logins race and the last write can restore a code the other request consumed—breaking the stated “used exactly once” contract and creating a security issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Backup codes are modeled as one encrypted JSON array in a nullable TEXT column with per-code state encoded as null sentinels inside the blob, instead of a child table with per-code hash and used_at. adjudication.rationale: The diff stores all backup codes as one encrypted JSON blob in `User.backupCodes` (TEXT) and, on login with a backup code, performs a decrypt → modify array element to `null` → re-encrypt → `prisma.user.update(...)` sequence in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`. This is a classic read-modify-write pattern with no transaction/optimistic locking, so concurrent login attempts can overwrite each other’s updates (lost-update race), potentially leaving a just-consumed code effectively unconsumed and reusable. The finding’s points about non-atomic per-code consumption and lack of per-code audit trail are also grounded in this design shown in the diff.

Meanwhile, the `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup` endpoint overwrites the stored `user.backupCodes` each time it is called (`backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes), ...)` in the prisma update). Therefore, if a second setup call occurs before the successful enable (e.g., another tab/window), the server-side codes can be replaced while this modal will still show/download/copy the earlier `backupCodes` state, creating a real risk of the user saving codes that do not match what is stored server-side.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The migration adds backupCodes as a nullable column with no backfill, so every user whose 2FA was enabled before this deploy has backupCodes = NULL, and the new Lost Access flow dead-ends for exactly those users: authorize throws MissingBackupCodes and the login page renders 'No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings.' — an instruction a locked-out user cannot follow. Pre-existing 2FA users who lose their authenticator click the new 'Lost access' button, submit a code, and are sent in circles by the only recovery affordance the UI offers (they cannot log in to reach settings, and no generate path exists while 2FA is enabled even when logged in); the same misleading message renders in DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx (lines 75-76) for codeless logged-in users, where it is confusing but recoverable via the TOTP path.

For users who already had `twoFactorEnabled=true` before this deploy, `backupCodes` will remain `NULL`. In the new Lost Access flow, next-auth `authorize` explicitly throws `MissingBackupCodes` when `user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode` but `!user.backupCodes`, and the login page maps that to `t("missing_backup_codes")` ("No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings."). That is a dead-end for locked-out users because this diff shows no alternate recovery path for already-enabled 2FA accounts beyond having backup codes or TOTP. The disable endpoint has the same `MissingBackupCodes` branch when `req.body.backupCode` is provided, reinforcing the issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The copy button calls navigator.clipboard.writeText(...) without awaiting it or attaching a rejection handler, then unconditionally shows the "backup codes copied!" success toast on the next line. When the clipboard write rejects (permission denied, document unfocused) the user is told the copy succeeded while it failed, and the rejection is unhandled; backup codes are displayed exactly once, so a user who trusts the toast and closes the dialog can permanently lose their recovery codes.

adjudication.rationale: In `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx` (DisplayBackupCodes step), the copy handler calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` and immediately calls `showToast(t("backup_codes_copied"), "success")` without `await`/`.then`/`.catch`. This can show a success toast even if the clipboard write fails (e.g., permissions, insecure context, unfocused document) and can also produce an unhandled promise rejection. The incorrect success feedback is directly introduced by the diff; the “permanently lose recovery codes” consequence is plausible given the UI flow but not strictly provable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] handleEnable replaces onEnable() with setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes), deferring the success signal to the backup-codes "close" button, while Escape/overlay dismissal exits the Dialog via onOpenChange only and never invokes onEnable (or resetState). Dismissing the dialog at the backup-codes step leaves the server with twoFactorEnabled=true while the parent is never notified and keeps showing 2FA as disabled; the natural recovery — clicking Enable again — re-runs the setup endpoint, which silently regenerates the TOTP secret and backup codes and invalidates the codes the user already saved.

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, handleEnable no longer calls onEnable() on success and instead does `setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes)` (diff shows `if (response.status === 200) { setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes); return; }`). At the DisplayBackupCodes step, the Cancel button is not rendered (`step !== SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes ? <Button ...>{t("cancel")}</Button> : null`), and the only path that calls `onEnable()`/`resetState()` is the explicit "close" button handler. The Dialog itself is still controlled via `open`/`onOpenChange` with no resetState or onEnable wiring on close, so dismissing via the dialog’s close mechanisms (overlay/escape, depending on Dialog implementation) would close without notifying the parent and without resetting local state. Given the server-side enable already happened before reaching DisplayBackupCodes, this can leave UI/parent out of sync and re-opening "Enable" would re-run setup, which (per setup.ts) regenerates and overwrites `twoFactorSecret` and `backupCodes`, invalidating previously saved codes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] authorize persists the consumed backup code (backupCodes[index] = null followed by prisma.user.update) before the credentials flow has actually produced a session. Any failure after the burn — an error in NextAuth's jwt/session callbacks, a dropped response, or the client dying before the session cookie is set — leaves the user logged out with that backup code permanently destroyed; the retry now returns IncorrectBackupCode, so recovery codes are burned by attempts that never yielded access, with no audit trail or way to restore them.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, the backup code is marked consumed and persisted immediately inside `authorize` (`backupCodes[index] = null; await prisma.user.update(...)`) before the request has definitively completed sign-in (cookie/session issuance happens after `authorize` returns in NextAuth). The diff does show this early, irreversible mutation. However, the specific failure modes cited (jwt/session callback errors, dropped response/client dying before cookie set) are outside what the diff can prove, so this is best treated as an architecture/edge-case concern rather than a directly verifiable defect in the changed code path itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The backup-code consumption is an unguarded read-modify-write (decrypt → indexOf → null → encrypt → update) with no transaction or compare-and-swap on the prior ciphertext. Two concurrent sign-ins using different valid codes both read the same stored list and the last write wins, restoring the first code into storage — a spent code silently remains valid and the stored state diverges from the codes actually used, breaking the "exactly once" promise the UI makes (double-submit races hit the same interleaving).

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, backup-code login performs a non-atomic read-modify-write: decrypt `user.backupCodes` → find index → set `backupCodes[index] = null` → re-encrypt → `prisma.user.update(...)`. There is no transaction and no conditional update (e.g., `where: { id, backupCodes: <previousCiphertext> }`), so two concurrent sign-ins can both read the same original ciphertext and then write back different modified versions; the last write can overwrite the other, effectively resurrecting a spent code and violating the “used exactly once” guarantee.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The backup-code verification block calls req.body.backupCode.replaceAll and JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, ...)) with no type guard and no error handling. A truthy non-string backupCode (number, object, or array in the JSON body) throws TypeError on .replaceAll, and an undecryptable or corrupt backupCodes blob (e.g. after encryption-key rotation) throws inside JSON.parse — both escape as an unhandled 500 with a non-JSON body instead of the 400 {error: ErrorCode} envelope the modal's error mapping expects, so the client's response.json() throws and the user lands in the generic catch message.

adjudication.rationale: In the new backup-code path in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the code assumes `req.body.backupCode` is a string and calls `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` after only checking truthiness (`if (user.twoFactorEnabled && req.body.backupCode)`). A truthy non-string (e.g., object/array) would throw a `TypeError`. The same block does `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, ...))` with no try/catch; if decryption fails or the decrypted value is not valid JSON, it will throw and bypass the intended `{ error: ErrorCode.* }` JSON response flow. The client code (`DisableTwoFactorModal`) unconditionally calls `response.json()`, so a non-JSON 500 response will itself throw and fall into the generic catch, matching the finding’s described user-visible behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Login compares the submitted backup code case-sensitively (Array.indexOf) against the lowercase hex codes produced by crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex"), while the BackupCode TextField sets no autocapitalize/autocorrect/spellcheck suppression. On mobile keyboards that auto-capitalize by default (iOS Safari), a code beginning with a-f is submitted uppercased and fails verification with "Backup code is incorrect" despite being valid — a false negative on the recovery path that the user cannot diagnose and that burns nothing but repeated attempts never explain.

adjudication.rationale: Backup codes are generated as lowercase hex strings in `setup.ts` (`crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")`). Both verification paths compare via `Array.indexOf()` against the user-supplied value with only `replaceAll("-", "")` applied (API disable endpoint: `backupCodes.indexOf(req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))`; next-auth authorize: `backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))`). No normalization like `.toLowerCase()` is performed. The `BackupCode` input (`apps/web/components/auth/BackupCode.tsx`) does not set `autoCapitalize="off"` / `autoCorrect="off"` / `spellCheck={false}`, so uppercasing by some mobile keyboards would cause valid codes containing a-f to be rejected as `IncorrectBackupCode`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The disable endpoint applies the same case-sensitive indexOf comparison against lowercase hex codes with no input normalization (no toLowerCase), matching the login-path gap. A user disabling 2FA via a hand-typed backup code from a mobile keyboard gets a false "Backup code is incorrect" error for a valid code, blocking the disable operation with an honest-looking but wrong error.

adjudication.rationale: In the new disable flow, backup codes are generated as lowercase hex (`crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")` in `totp/setup.ts`). But the disable endpoint checks membership with a case-sensitive `indexOf` on the stored array: `backupCodes.indexOf(req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))` (`totp/disable.ts`) without normalizing case. If a user enters an otherwise valid code with uppercase A-F (common with mobile auto-capitalization), the lookup will fail and return `IncorrectBackupCode`, preventing 2FA disable via backup code.
